site.name: al-Marṣad
page.title: Ask the graph
page.description: Ask a question in plain words and see what the graph records, with the claim behind each row and how far it has been checked.
page.lead: Ask about the people, events and places in the graph. The answer lists what the graph records, with the claim behind each row and how far each claim has been checked.
page.how: How it works: fixed rules turn your question into a query you can read and edit. The query runs on a copy of the graph in your browser. No AI model is used, and nothing you type is sent anywhere.
page.label: Your question
page.placeholder: For example: Who was at both Badr and Uhud?
page.load_failed: The graph could not be loaded, so questions cannot be answered here right now. The answered questions below still work.
page.nojs: Typing a question needs JavaScript. Without it, you can read the questions already answered below.
page.cached_lead: Each links to the full answer. The answers are rebuilt from the graph every time the site is built.
page.cached_check: These questions and their expected answers are checked automatically on every build. The expected answers are pending a scholar's check.
page.limits_heading: What this tool will not do
page.limits_lead: Some questions are refused on purpose, with the reason. The rules are the project's own:
page.coverage: The graph holds {person} people, {group} groups, {event} events, {story} stories and {place} places.
page.coverage_status: {proposed} claims are recorded but not yet reviewed by scholars, and {accepted} have been accepted. Another {none} links, such as who took part in an event, carry no review status of their own.
page.coverage_gaps: What the graph says it does not cover yet
cached.note: This answer was built from the graph when the site was built. On the ask page the same question runs live, in your browser.
want.target: an event or a story, or an events(...) query
want.set: a list query, such as participants(...) or events(...)
want.entity: an entry: a person, group, place, event or story
want.happening_or_place: an event, a story or a place
want.dated: an event, a story or a person
want.year: a year, such as 5 AH or 627 CE
plain.participants: people and groups recorded as taking part in {target}
plain.people_range: people and groups recorded in events at {place}, {range}
plain.connected_any: people and groups with a recorded tie to {agent}, or recorded in the same event
plain.connected_ties: people and groups with a recorded tie to {agent}
plain.connected_events: people and groups recorded in the same events as {agent}
plain.between_place: claims that link {a} with {b}, or with events recorded there
plain.path: the shortest chain of recorded claims from {a} to {b}, at most {max} steps
plain.when_death: the recorded date of death of {x}
plain.except: those in the first list but not the second: {a}; but not {b}
plain.reviewed: {set}, counting only claims accepted by scholars

answer.lead.agents.other: The graph records {n} people and groups that match.
answer.lead.events.one: The graph records one event that matches.
answer.lead.events.other: The graph records {n} events that match.
answer.lead.stories.one: The graph records one story that matches.
answer.lead.stories.other: The graph records {n} stories that match.
answer.lead.places.one: The graph records one place that matches.
answer.lead.places.other: The graph records {n} places that match.
answer.status_none: None of the claims behind this answer has been reviewed by scholars yet: each is recorded, not yet reviewed.
answer.status_some: {a} of the {n} claims behind this answer have been accepted by scholars; the rest are recorded, not yet reviewed.
answer.status_all: All {n} claims behind this answer have been accepted by scholars.
answer.empty: The graph records nothing that matches.
answer.empty_why: That does not mean it did not happen. The graph is small and not yet reviewed: it holds {person} people, {event} events, {place} places and {story} stories, a small part of the Companions' generation.
answer.gaps: What the graph says it does not cover:
answer.overlaps: recorded date too broad to tell
answer.more: Showing {shown} of {n}. The rest are on the pages of the entries named in the question.
answer.alts: Other entries with a similar name to “{mention}”:
answer.path_lead.one: The graph links {a} and {b} in one step:
answer.path_lead.other: The graph links {a} and {b} in {n} steps:
answer.path_none: The graph has no chain of up to {max} recorded claims from {a} to {b}.
answer.links_lead.one: The graph records one claim that links {a} with {b}:
answer.links_lead.other: The graph records {n} claims that link {a} with {b}:
answer.links_none: The graph records no claim that links {a} with {b}.
answer.dates_none: The graph records no date for {x}.
answer.field_status: Status: part of the entry, no review status of its own
answer.about_lead.one: {x} has a page in the graph. One claim touches it:
answer.about_lead.other: {x} has a page in the graph. {n} claims touch it:
answer.about_none: {x} has a page in the graph, but no claim touches it yet.
claim.ai: From a document generated with AI; its authenticity is unknown.
status.label: Status: {value}
status.proposed: proposed (recorded, not yet reviewed by scholars)
status.none: not recorded (no review is recorded for this link)
note.time_ah.one: Years in AH are turned into dates with the tabular Islamic calendar, so the edges of the period may be off by a day.
note.time_overlaps.one: One of these has a recorded date too broad to tell whether it falls inside the period. It is marked.
note.time_overlaps.other: {n} of these have recorded dates too broad to tell whether they fall inside the period. They are marked.
note.time_undated.one: One event with no recorded date was left out.
note.time_undated.other: {n} events with no recorded date were left out.
note.time_undated_direct.one: One claim about the place itself carries no date and was left out.
note.time_undated_direct.other: {n} claims about the place itself carry no date and were left out.
note.time_assumed_ah.one: A year written without AH or CE is read as AH.
note.left_out.one: One claim rejected or replaced by scholars was left out.
note.left_out.other: {n} claims rejected or replaced by scholars were left out.
note.story_list.one: The people of a story are the ones its list names. The list comes from the 50 Stories document, which was generated with AI and has not been reviewed. Read each role: a list can name someone who did not take part, for example because they were absent or on the other side.
note.same_event.one: Being recorded in the same event does not show that two people met.
note.people_at.one: Recorded at a place means recorded as taking part in an event there, or named in a claim about the place itself, such as “died at” or “migrated to”.
note.path.one: Each step is a separate recorded claim. A chain of records is not a relationship in history.
note.fields.one: Dates are recorded as part of the entry, not as separate claims, so they have no review status of their own.
note.except.one: Not being in the second list only means the graph records no such claim.
note.count.one: This counts records in the graph, not people in history.
note.reviewed.one: Only claims accepted by scholars are counted.
note.gender.one: The graph does not record whether a person is male or female, so every recorded child or sibling is listed.
refusal.heading: Not answered
refusal.ruling.reason: This tool does not give religious rulings (fatwa), and it cannot say what is permitted or forbidden.
refusal.ruling.offer: Please ask a qualified scholar. What the tool can do is show what the graph records about people, events and places, with the source and review status of each claim.
refusal.interpretation.reason: This tool does not interpret the Qur'an or hadith, or draw lessons from them.
refusal.interpretation.offer: That is the work of qualified scholars. The tool can show where and when the graph records an event, and who it records as present.
refusal.grading.reason: This tool does not grade reports or hadith, and it does not say whether a report is authentic.
refusal.grading.offer: Grading is an act by named scholars. Where the graph records one, the report's page shows it with who made it. Each claim here shows only how far it has been reviewed.
refusal.fabrication.reason: This tool never writes hadith, reports, sayings or stories about the Prophet ﷺ or the Companions, under any framing.
refusal.fabrication.offer: Everything it shows comes from the graph's records, with their sources. Try asking who is recorded at an event, or which stories name a person.
refusal.depiction.reason: No pictures of the Prophet ﷺ, his family or the Companions are made or shown here, in any form, and the tool does not describe how anyone looked.
refusal.depiction.offer: The site shows people as names, places and the lines between them.
refusal.ranking.reason: This tool does not rank people by greatness, piety or importance, and it does not turn counts of records into rankings.
refusal.ranking.offer: A count of records measures the record, not the person. The tool can list what the graph records about each person, with sources.
refusal.speculation.reason: This tool does not guess what probably happened, or fill gaps in the record.
refusal.speculation.offer: It shows only what is recorded, and says where the record is silent.
refusal.judgement.reason: This tool does not pass religious or moral judgement on anyone, or decide who was right in a dispute.
refusal.judgement.offer: Where scholars disagree, the graph records the positions and who holds them, without choosing between them.
refusal.limit.interpretation: No interpretation of the Qur'an or hadith.
refusal.limit.grading: No grading of reports or hadith.
refusal.limit.fabrication: No writing of hadith, reports or stories.
refusal.limit.depiction: No pictures or descriptions of how people looked.
refusal.limit.ranking: No ranking of people, and no counts turned into rankings.
refusal.limit.judgement: No judgement of people, and no deciding disputes.
unsupported.heading: Not understood yet
unsupported.generic: This question is outside what the tool can answer so far. It knows a fixed set of question shapes, and this one matches none of them.
unsupported.time_needs_place: A period of time can only be used with events or with a place, as in “What happened in Makkah between 1 and 8 AH?”.
unsupported.time_era: Please give the years with AH or CE, as in “between 1 and 5 AH”.
unsupported.time_bh: Years before the Hijra cannot be searched yet.
unsupported.reviewed_needs_list: “Reviewed only” works with questions whose answer is a list, as in “Who was at Badr, reviewed claims only?”.
ambiguous.heading: Which one?
ambiguous.lead: “{mention}” matches {n} entries in the graph. Choose one:
ambiguous.more: Some matches are not shown; type more of the name.
notfound.heading: Not in the graph
notfound.lead: The graph has no {kinds} that matches “{mention}”.
invalid.heading: The query could not run
toolong.lead: The question is too long. Please keep it under {max} characters.
error.unterminated: A quoted name is not closed.
error.character: The query has a character it cannot read: “{near}”.
error.trailing: There is unexpected text at the end of the query: “{near}”.
error.too_deep: The query is nested too deeply.
error.positional: {op}: an unnamed value comes after a named one.
error.not_found: No {kind} in the graph is named “{label}”.
error.ambiguous: {n} entries of kind {kind} are named “{label}”; use the ID instead.
error.year: The year {year} is outside the range this tool accepts.
error.steps: max must be a number from 1 to {max}.
error.not_op: A query must start with an operation, such as participants(...).
error.too_many: The query has too many operations.
error.filter: {op} needs at least one filter: at, involving, from or to.
error.range: The start year comes after the end year.
error.same: Both ends of the path are the same entry.
error.mixed: {op} needs two lists of the same kind.
